items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Of course, he had played with other bands before -- Snookum Russell. But he came with us not long after he had left Andy Kirk's band. His name was Fats Navarro

ctx.x: Well, Fats came in the band after Dizzy. Dizzy stayed with the band until January of 1945. By this time, he felt like he was strong enough to do some things on his own. He had offers from agents in New York to do things. I guess, name-wise, he was the most popular instrumentalist in the band. Because Dizzy had been around for a while, he had played with a lot of bands and he'd made quite a few records with different people, and he was a well-known musician.

So Dizzy left the band in January of 1945, and we got this trumpet player who had been formerly with Andy Kirk's band. Of course, he had played with other bands before -- Snookum Russell. But he came with us not long after he had left Andy Kirk's band. His name was Fats Navarro -- at least,
